description: Phase 2 parity: a failed capture while the permission report says Automation is not granted switches the same panel window to onboarding (its steps listed, nothing opened); with Automation granted (all granted, or only Accessibility missing) the failure stays on route capture (phase failed, the failure message shown)
requirement: P2-capture-permission-route (GPUI Phase 2 parity, Tauri dist/panel.js capture-err handler)
notes: Tauri reference: dist/panel.js onEvent('capture-err'): show the failure, then read the permission report; only `report && !canUseCapture(report)` (Automation not 'granted') routes to onboarding. A transient capture error with Automation granted, or with no report at all, stays on the capture view.

The report comes from the `permission` fixture, the same file the onboarding view reads (crate::fixtures::path(Fixture::Permission), views/onboarding.rs check_permissions). The capture path must consult that same report; automation builds never run the osascript probe.

The no-report case (capture fails, no permission fixture loaded: stay on capture, phase failed, message shown) is capture-view.json's second half and is not repeated here; this scenario must not contradict it.
Round 1 uses permissions-two-missing.json (automation 'denied'): the route switches to onboarding in the SAME window (window_id saved before and compared after) and process, and nothing is opened.

Round 2 restarts for a fresh instance (restart replays both setup fixtures), THEN loads permissions-all-granted.json so it overrides the replayed two-missing report. 'Stays on capture' is checked after a 1 s settle, so a late async route switch cannot pass it.

Round 3 restarts again and loads permissions-accessibility-missing.json (accessibility false, automation 'granted'): only Automation decides the route (Tauri canUseCapture, 'Defect 5: capture needs only Automation'), so a missing Accessibility grant alone must NOT route to onboarding. This rules out routing on 'any permission missing' or on Accessibility.
